method: Six-axis live-source sweep (Anthropic / OpenAI / Google+xAI / open-weight / benchmarks / harness binding), each axis independently fact-checked by an adversarial pass instructed to refute; only vendor-page-confirmed ids and values were promoted here. Corrections applied included one fabricated model id, one shut-down model presented as current, and several mis-attributed benchmark sources. 2026-08-01 structural adjustment (not a data re-sweep): the T1.5 · Frontier Execution band was split out of T1 — the 2026-07-25 sweep recorded the 2x intra-T1 price spread ($10/$50 vs $5/$25) but the tier boundary absorbed it, and a temperament axis (think-to-action latency) surfaced in dogfood that the price rows do not carry. claude-opus-5 moved T1 → T1.5, and a per-account entitlement-check rule was added for invitation-gated models (claude-mythos-5). 2026-09-02 refresh — ANTHROPIC AXIS ONLY, triggered by the 2026-09-01 Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 launch (revisit rule (c): new flagship). Re-derived from the vendor models-overview, per-model overview, what's-new, migration-guide, pricing, model-deprecations and Claude Code model-config pages fetched the same day; two dated watchlist items were re-baselined (Sonnet 5 introductory pricing made permanent; Opus 4.1 retired 2026-08-05 with zero pins found in this estate). OpenAI, Google, xAI and open-weight rows were NOT re-swept in this pass and carry their 2026-07-25 / 2026-08-16 values; their watchlist items stand unverified. 2026-09-05 refresh, four axes, each run as two independent collectors plus one adversarial verifier that re-opened every cited URL and marked each field confirmed / unconfirmed / contradicted: Google Flash line (gemini-3.8-flash added, 3.7 Flash demoted to previous-generation), OpenAI (gpt-6-astra added; the entire gpt-5.6 family was found repriced on 2026-07-30 and is corrected here — neither collector looked at the sibling rows while standing on the pricing page), Anthropic Fable 5.1 delta (the Claude Code changelog for 2.1.257–2.1.261 was transcribed verbatim after both collectors mis-versioned three Fable-specific fixes when they summarized it), and harness binding (the Claude Code subagent model resolution order was found REVERSED since v2.1.251 — this registry carried the pre-reversal order through three refreshes because a version-range delta cannot see drift that entered before the range; Codex CLI 0.153.4 moved the bundled default to Astra). One standing claim was contradicted by the vendor page and re-baselined: the Google 2.5-family shutdown 2026-10-16 appears on no row of the deprecations page as of 2026-09-05. xAI and open-weight rows were NOT re-swept and remain on their 2026-07-25 / 2026-08-16 values.

tiers.definition: The vendor's deepest-reasoning flagship, highest cost per token, thinking on by default and often not disableable. Characterized by sustained multi-hour autonomy, self-verification before acting, and the widest reasoning-effort ladder (including a top rung the cheaper tiers lack). Today: claude-fable-5, gpt-5.6-sol, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, grok-4.5, kimi-k3; gated members: claude-mythos-5 (restricted access), gpt-5.5-pro (escalation-only).
tiers.selectionIntent: Select when the cost of a wrong answer exceeds the cost of the tokens: irreversible actions, ambiguous or under-specified inputs, architecture that later work will be built on, and adversarial review of another model's output. Do NOT select for volume — its per-token price is the tier's defining constraint, and vendor guidance is that a larger model can be cheaper per finished task only when the task is genuinely hard.

tiers.definition: The vendor's start-here flagship: frontier-class capability at roughly half T1 per-token price, positioned by the vendor itself as the default for complex agentic coding rather than for deepest deliberation. Split from T1 on temperament as much as price: it converts thinking into action sooner — speed on well-framed work, a slip risk on under-framed work. Today: claude-opus-5. Vendors without a separate id here may span the band with a mode switch instead (gpt-5.6-sol reasoning.mode standard|pro) — such rows stay in T1 until measured.
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for complex multi-step execution where judgment remains but the frame is already set: the daily-driver main loop, heavyweight implementation lanes, subagent leads. Always pair it with explicit verification gates (check-first, test gates) — the observed failure mode is premature action, and raising effort does not buy deliberation here. Escalate to T1 for architecture, ambiguous requirements, and adversarial review; drop to T2 once the spec is complete. Not a verification tier: adversarial review stays T1, cross-family.

tiers.definition: The workhorse: near-frontier coding capability at roughly a third to a half of T1 per-token cost, tuned for tool loops and multi-file edits, with a full effort ladder and a large (≥400K, usually ~1M) context window. Today: claude-sonnet-5 / claude-opus-4-8, gpt-5.6-terra, gemini-3.6-flash / gemini-3.5-flash, grok-4.3, glm-5.2, deepseek-v4-pro.
tiers.selectionIntent: The default tier for the main coding loop once the decision is already made and the spec is written. Select whenever the work is 'do the thing correctly' rather than 'decide what the thing is'. This is where a maintainer should spend most tokens; escalation to T1 should be the exception you can name a reason for.

tiers.definition: Cheap-but-competent models the vendor itself markets for subagents and fan-out — real code edits and real tool use, but a smaller window or a shallower reasoning ceiling than T2. Typically 5-15x cheaper on output than T1. Today: gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.4-mini, grok-build-0.1, deepseek-v4-flash.
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for wide parallel lanes where the unit of work is small, independently verifiable, and cheap to redo: read-heavy scans, large-file review, per-file mechanical edits, test scaffolding. The economic point of this tier is that a failed lane is cheap to re-run, so buy width instead of depth.

tiers.definition: The cheapest always-on tier: sub-$1 input, minimal or off-by-default thinking, lowest latency floor. Marketed for classification, extraction, routing and watch loops rather than authoring. Often has NO effort parameter at all (claude-haiku-4-5) or defaults to none/minimal (gpt-5.4-nano, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-2.5-flash-lite). Today: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, gpt-5.4-nano, gemini-3.5-flash-lite / gemini-3.1-flash-lite / gemini-2.5-flash-lite.
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for anything that must run continuously and mostly return 'nothing to do': inbox/board polling, event classification, triage routing, digest extraction. Budget it as a fixed monthly cost, not per-task. Never let this tier author code or make a routing decision that is expensive to reverse — its job is to decide whether to wake a higher tier.

aliases: claude-fable-5-1 (the dateless id is its own pinned snapshot; the alias row repeats it)

Claude Code: `fable` → «the latest Fable model for your hardest and longest-running tasks»; `best` → «the latest Fable model where it's available to you, otherwise the same model as `opus`» (v2.1.255+) — EXCEPT in Claude apps gateway sessions, where v2.1.257 changed `fable` and `best` to keep resolving to Fable 5 «for now, since gateways not yet configured for Fable 5.1 reject it»; there, pick Fable 5.1 explicitly in `/model`. Don't read a `best`/`fable` lane as «running 5.1» without checking the session's provider — the alias silently means a different model, and a different cache-read price, behind a gateway.
models.contextWindow: 1M input (default AND maximum, standard per-token price across the whole window) / 128k max output. NOT on the vendor's Batch-API output-300k list (that list names Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 4.6 only). Tokenizer = Fable 5 = the Opus 4.7 line (~30% more tokens than pre-4.7 models for the same text). Claude Code v2.1.260 changed auto-compact for 1M-context models so «Opus and Fable sessions now compact shortly before the 1M-token limit», and stopped recovery compaction on very large contexts timing out at 10 minutes; before that a 1M lane compacted against the older threshold. Same release fixed `model: fable` subagents ignoring the `[1m]` tag on an `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` pin and «silently running with a 200K context window» — on ≤2.1.259 a `[1m]`-pinned fan-out lane is not the window it claims to be, and nothing in the transcript says so. Don't infer the effective window from the pin; it is a silent downgrade.
models.pricingPerMTok: $10 input / $50 output — same as Fable 5. Cache write $12.50 (5m) / $20 (1h). Cache read $0.25 = 0.025× base (a quarter of Fable 5's $1; every other Claude model is 0.1×). Batch $5 / $25. inference_geo:"us" ×1.1 on all categories. Priority Tier: NOT supported (Fable 5 is). Fast mode: not offered (Opus 5 / 4.8 only). Vendor's own aggregate framing (2026-09-01 announcement): «Fable 5.1 will cost an estimated 25% less than Fable 5 for typical workloads, wherever usage is billed by token», «For highly agentic work, the savings will often be much larger—up to approximately 45%», «Cache reads now cost 75% less, or $0.25 per million tokens». Every dollar of that saving lives in cache reads alone — base input, output, cache writes and batch are byte-identical to Fable 5 — so a lane that misses the cache saves exactly nothing and the 25%/45% figures do not apply to it. Two consequences worth acting on: (a) the vendor now advises compacting LATER, not earlier — «Because cache reads are now cheaper, compacting early to save cost may no longer be the right cost-intelligence tradeoff on Claude Fable 5.1, so experiment with later compaction points»; (b) Claude Code BEFORE v2.1.260 did not cache the context attached after tool results on Fable 5.1 and re-sent it as uncached input on every tool-call turn — an agentic session on v2.1.255–2.1.259 (this workspace's recorded v2.1.258 included) pays $10/MTok where it should pay $0.25. Don't benchmark Fable 5.1 cost on a pre-2.1.260 harness; upgrade first, then measure.
models.effort: output_config.effort = low | medium | high (default) | xhigh | max. Thinking ALWAYS ON — thinking:{type:"disabled"} and {type:"enabled",budget_tokens:N} both 400; non-default temperature/top_p/top_k 400; assistant prefill 400. Per-message effort change WITHOUT cache invalidation: beta header mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01, an effort-only {role:"system", content:[], output_config:{effort}} entry in messages (also Mythos 5.1 and Opus 5; Claude API). Vendor calibration: «At medium, results roughly match Claude Fable 5 at lower cost»; «At low, Claude Fable 5.1 is often competitive with Claude Opus and Claude Sonnet models on cost per task while scoring higher» — re-run the effort sweep even if one exists for Fable 5 (level names do not carry across models). Effort-specific shifts: at low it calls search/retrieval less and answers from memory more; at xhigh/max it may draft a long deliverable in thinking and again in the reply (set max_tokens for thinking+reply, or stay at high). models.notes: Released 2026-09-01. Vendor: «For demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work» — «or when your evals on Claude Opus 5 at higher effort still fall short»; the vendor's start-here model stays Opus 5. Latency «Slower»; single requests can run many minutes. Reliable knowledge cutoff Jun 2026 (training cutoff Jun 2026). Status Active (latest); retirement not sooner than 2027-09-01. Successor to Fable 5 in the same tier at the same per-token price; migration is «mostly drop-in» with THREE BREAKING CHANGES: ① forced tool use — tool_choice {type:"any"} / {type:"tool"} return 400 «tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.» (also on Batches and count_tokens) → keep auto + name the tool in the prompt, strict:true for schema-valid args, or structured outputs; ② thinking blocks are bound to the producing model — Fable 5.1 reads earlier models' blocks, no earlier model reads 5.1's; a router/fallback that moves the conversation off 5.1 drops them silently and unbilled (beta thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 reports drops in input_transformations); ③ editing anything before a 5.1 thinking block (system, tools, an earlier message, injected-then-removed reminders, a URL serving different bytes) invalidates every later block → 400 «The block is bound to a different conversation» — ENFORCED for accounts created on/after 2026-08-31, record-only for older accounts unless thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior is set; safe operations: dropping a leading run of thinking blocks, server-side compaction/context editing, moving cache_control, changing effort. Mythos 5.1 does NOT run check ③. FIVE ADDITIVE: per-message effort (see effort); turn-scoped system messages clear_at:"next_user_message" (beta mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21 — the vendor's replacement for inject-and-delete reminders; cleared copies cost 0 input tokens and must stay in the array byte-for-byte); thinking.display:"updates" (beta thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18) returns between-tool-call progress notes as text while reasoning stays hidden (default display is still "omitted" = empty blocks = silent-looking agent); cache reads at $0.25; content provenance — every text output carries Anthropic's statistical watermark on every platform, image/video files via Files API carry signed C2PA credentials (no tokens added, no change to requests). Refusals: same stop_details categories as Fable 5 («fewer false positives than Claude Fable 5's did at launch, and finding vulnerabilities in source code is permitted»); fallbacks:"default" (beta) retries a declined request on the category's recommended model — permitted targets Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 (Claude Code: cybersecurity → Opus 4.8, biology → Opus 5; togglable via switchModelsOnFlag); a refusal before any output is not billed and fallback credit refunds the cache-switch cost. Data: 30-day retention required, designated Covered Model, no ZDR unless expressly authorized (a request from a ZDR org/workspace returns 400 invalid_request_error). Platforms: Claude API, Amazon Bedrock (anthropic.claude-fable-5-1), Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry — note Opus 5 shows «—» for Claude Platform on AWS while 5.1 is listed. BEHAVIOR SHIFTS vs Fable 5 (vendor-documented, each with a prompt fix — see harnessProfile): parallel tool calling more variable when the next reads are only implied by a coding/computer-use loop; fewer user-facing progress updates, more so at high effort; denser prose in places; less bold/headers/lists in chat (anti-formatting rules written for older models now suppress needed structure); unmarked quotations in summaries; whole-file rewrites for small edits. Claude Code: reach via /model fable (or `best`), never the account default on any plan or provider, minimum Claude Code v2.1.255, may bill usage credits depending on plan/seat («Requires usage credits» in the picker; interactive sessions ask consent), hidden under ZDR; settings pinned to `claude-fable-5` are auto-rewritten to the `fable` alias on first run of v2.1.255+. Vendor pages used: overview · what's-new · migration guide · pricing · model-deprecations · Claude Code model-config (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-1/whats-new-fable-5-1 · https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-1/migration-guide · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config). 2026-09-05 delta pass. PROMPTING: the vendor ships a dedicated page, «Prompting Claude Fable 5.1» (16 sections), and it carries fixes the model page does not list: «Finish the whole task» (the model stops to ask «Shall I apply this?» or narrates the next step instead of doing it; the vendor's two-block system prompt opens «You are operating autonomously. The user is not watching in real time and cannot answer questions mid-task» and that sentence «carries much of the effect»), «Keep changes and tests to what the task asks for» (unrequested adjacent fixes and committed test files «drop substantially with no measurable change in task success»), «Tell the model what to preserve in compaction summaries» (a six-item preservation list; server-side compaction already does this, so it is a client-compaction fix only), «Let the lead agent keep working while subagents run» (a start-subagent tool that returns immediately + results delivered as a later user message + a separate wait tool «lowers average time to completion at similar quality, token usage, and cost»), «Give vision work tools to crop and zoom», «Consider all effort levels», and «Reduce safeguard false positives» with three named triggers — compile-check phrasing (ask «Are there any bugs in this program?», not «Does this program compile without errors?»), lesser-known programming languages (give the model the language's documentation), and base64-encoded data in tool output (remove it). DON'T paste those prompt blocks into a harness that already says the same thing — «Finish the whole task» duplicates this workspace's autonomy rule and «Keep changes to what the task asks for» duplicates its scope rule; doubling a system prompt buys nothing and lengthens the cached prefix. PRESERVED-THINKING SCOPE NARROWED: the vendor states «Claude Code, claude.ai, Claude Managed Agents, and the Claude Agent SDK keep that prefix intact for you», so breaking change ③ is a risk for code that builds the `messages` array itself, NOT for lanes running inside those harnesses — don't spend a probe cycle proving the harness safe. Sharpening: «Removing a thinking block from anywhere other than the start of the run invalidates every thinking block after it.» SAFEGUARDS, QUANTIFIED (announcement page, not the docs): «In cybersecurity, our newest safeguards block 60% fewer false positives than before», «Claude Code users can expect an average of around 60% fewer interventions per session from our cyber safeguards», and biology safeguards «fire 85% less often for benign requests related to elementary biology and medical questions» — read that last one carefully: it is scoped to «Fable 5.1 and Fable 5», so it is a safeguard-generation improvement, not a 5.1-over-5 differentiator. A system card («Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1») is linked from the announcement; not read this pass, publication date unverified. RE-VERIFIED UNCHANGED 2026-09-05: the id `claude-fable-5-1`; every price including the 0.025× cache-read multiplier (now also stated on the general pricing page, so it is vendor-canonical rather than one page's artifact); the four platforms with their exact ids; Active with «Not sooner than September 1, 2027»; and no new Anthropic deprecation notice of any kind — the newest entry in the deprecation history is still 2026-06-05 (Opus 4.1). Claude Code's highest published version on 2026-09-05 is v2.1.261; there is no 2.1.262+.

Do NOT stand up an unattended long-horizon Astra lane without a mid-run 403 handler and a subscription to that alert: the failure mode is a live agent halted mid-task, not a rejected request at submit time. effortGuidance: Default first, escalate on evidence — not on principle. Anthropic's own Claude Code guidance is "For most tasks you should use the model's default effort level", and to "Pick a higher effort level if Claude got it wrong by skipping a file, not running the tests, or not double-checking its work." Escalation should be traceable to an observed failure mode, not to the importance of the task.

NON-MONOTONICITY IS VENDOR-DOCUMENTED, not folklore. Claude Code's effort table says of max: "Can improve performance on demanding tasks but may show diminishing returns and is prone to overthinking. Test before adopting broadly." The API docs are blunter for the Opus 4.7/4.8 line: "On most workloads max adds significant cost for relatively small quality gains, and on some structured-output or less intelligence-sensitive tasks it can lead to overthinking." A blanket always-max policy is therefore a documented anti-pattern, not merely expensive.

Effort level names are NOT comparable across models: "The effort scale is calibrated per model, so the same level name does not represent the same underlying value across models." Any harness that stores one global effort setting and applies it to whatever model is active is storing a meaningless number — bind effort per model, as Claude Code does with per-subagent and per-skill `effort` frontmatter.

Carried-over settings are actively harmful after a model change. Anthropic on Opus 5: "If you carried effort settings over from an earlier model, run a fresh effort sweep on your evals rather than reusing them." This bites hardest in Claude Code, where Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 HOLD their default effort until you make an explicit choice, but Opus 5 has no such hold — a level you set for another model silently carries over.

Step DOWN the ladder before stepping across tiers. Vendor guidance for Fable 5: "Lower effort settings on Claude Fable 5 still perform well and often exceed xhigh performance on prior models." And for Sonnet 5, medium is "Comparable to Claude Sonnet 4.6 at high effort." A generation bump usually means the cheap rung of the new model beats the expensive rung of the old one — check that before downgrading tier.

Low effort is the intended subagent setting, and it changes tool behavior, not just prose. The effort docs list low's typical use as "Simpler tasks that need the best speed and lowest costs, such as subagents", and state that lower effort makes the model "Combine multiple operations into fewer tool calls" and "Make fewer tool calls". In a search or exploration lane, tool-call count is the dominant cost term, so low effort saves more than the token delta suggests.

Effort is a behavioral signal, not a token budget: "At lower effort levels, Claude will still think on sufficiently difficult problems, but it will think less than it would at higher effort levels for the same problem." You cannot use effort as a hard cost cap — pair it with max_tokens, and conversely at xhigh/max the docs tell you to set a LARGE max_tokens ("Starting at 64k tokens") or the model runs out of room mid-thought.

Effort is a caching decision as much as a quality decision: "Changing the effort value between requests invalidates prompt caching, so vary effort across workloads rather than within a conversation that relies on cache hits." For a long resident session, pick one level at session start and hold it; dynamic per-turn effort tuning can cost more than it saves.

On Opus 5, do not use effort to control verbosity — "changing effort does not reliably shorten responses, so prompt for length instead." Harnesses that lowered effort to cut output size on older models will see the cost saving without the brevity, and Opus 5 is separately reported to narrate more than 4.8 by default.

Know the two default-effort exceptions before you trust a default. In Claude Code "The default effort is high on every model that supports effort, except Opus 4.7, which defaults to xhigh." On the OpenAI side the exception runs the other way: gpt-5.4-mini and gpt-5.4-nano default reasoning.effort to `none`, so omitting the parameter gives you a non-reasoning model on a code-editing lane.

Anthropic's cheap tier has NO effort knob at all: claude-haiku-4-5 rejects the effort parameter and has no adaptive thinking. That asymmetry is a routing constraint, not a detail — if your resident-observer lane needs a dial, Google's Flash-Lite line (minimal/low/medium/high) or gpt-5.4-nano gives you one and Haiku does not.

On Google, effort control is now the ONLY supported determinism knob: the 2026-07-21 changelog deprecated temperature, top_p and top_k in the Gemini API. Any harness pinning temperature for reproducible output must migrate to thinking_level.

xAI has no low end of the ladder: for grok-4.5 the values are low, medium, high (default high) and "Reasoning cannot be disabled" — there is no none/minimal rung, so xAI cannot serve a true resident-observer lane on effort alone. Separately, on grok-4.20-multi-agent, effort selects AGENT COUNT (4 or 16) rather than reasoning depth, which makes xhigh there a 16x token multiplier rather than a deeper single pass. UPDATE 2026-08-16: grok-4.6 adds "xhigh" ABOVE high (default still high) — the ladder grew at the top, and the bottom is still missing: there is no none/minimal anywhere in xAI's lineup, so T3/T4-style minimal-effort lanes still cannot be expressed on xAI models.

`ultracode` and `ultrathink` are not effort levels and should not be modelled as such. Ultracode "is a Claude Code setting rather than a model effort level: it sends xhigh to the model and additionally has Claude orchestrate dynamic workflows", is session-only, and is rejected by both the persisted effortLevel setting and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. Ultrathink "adds an in-context instruction" and "The effort level sent to the API is unchanged" — so it costs nothing at the API-parameter layer and changes nothing there either.

A T1 main inherits into every fan-out lane by default, and on Fable 5.1 that default is the expensive failure mode. Claude Code (v2.1.251+) resolves a subagent's model as per-invocation `model` → frontmatter `model` → CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (a default, not a pin) → the main conversation's model, and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (v2.1.257+) overrides all of them — including bindings a guard just approved, which is why the reference guard reads that variable, and a Workflow lane that omits opts.model does the same — so with Fable 5.1 as main, an unbound research fan-out runs at $10/$50 with $0.25 cache reads it mostly cannot use (each lane starts cache-cold). The vendor's own guidance points the other way twice: Opus 5 is «the model the docs tell you to start with», and on Fable 5.1 «At low … often competitive with Claude Opus and Claude Sonnet models on cost per task while scoring higher» — i.e. when Fable IS the right lane, its cheap rung is the first thing to try, and `ultracode` (which sends xhigh) is a session setting that a lane inherits unless bound. Registry-level rule (2026-09-02): bind model AND effort on every lane; T1 only for lanes whose failure cost justifies it (architecture, ambiguous requirements, final adversarial review); never let a T1 × xhigh|max lane exist by inheritance. Reference mechanism: a PreToolUse guard that reads the session model and denies unbound Agent/Workflow lanes (plugins/superscalar/reference/lane-model-guard.cjs). Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config · https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-1

Sonnet 4.6 at 1M needs credits on every plan including Max.

Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform resolved `default` to Sonnet 4.5 before v2.1.207. Claude Code — subagent model resolution order (this is where a tiered-composition policy actually lands): CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL → per-invocation `model` parameter → subagent frontmatter `model` → main conversation's model. Frontmatter accepts sonnet/opus/haiku/fable, a full id, or `inherit` (the default), and a separate `effort` frontmatter field overrides the session level while that subagent runs. Note the built-in Explore agent no longer forces Haiku: as of v2.1.198 it inherits the main model, capped at Opus on the Claude API — define a project subagent named Explore with `model: haiku` to put exploration back on a cheap lane. Concurrency default is 20 subagents per session (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS), and ultracode sessions are exempt from that limit.

Claude Code — fast mode: Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 only, at $10/$50 per MTok for up to ~2.5x output tokens/sec. Heavily gated: an API research preview needing the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header plus account-manager/waitlist access; in Claude Code it requires usage credits turned on, draws from credits from the first token even when plan usage remains, needs Owner enablement on Team/Enterprise, is CLI-only (not the VS Code extension), and is unavailable on Bedrock/Google Cloud/Foundry/Claude Platform on AWS. Enable at session start — the first enable re-bills the whole context at fast-mode uncached input price. Opus 4.7 fast mode was REMOVED 2026-07-24 while Claude Code still treats 4.7 as fast-mode-capable, so /fast on 4.7 produces API rejections.

Codex — Plus ($20/mo): gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini. Roughly 15-90 Sol messages per 5-hour window scaling to ~60-350 on Luna. This is the tier where Sol-on-every-lane is not viable — a wide fan-out must run Terra or Luna.

Codex — Pro ($100/mo 5x, $200/mo 20x): everything on Plus plus gpt-5.3-codex-spark (research preview, Pro only, ChatGPT-surfaces only, separately rate-limited). ~75-450 Sol messages (5x) to ~300-1,800 (20x) per 5-hour window — the first tier with real headroom for many-subagent operation.

Codex — Business ($25/user/mo, min 2): the same roster as Plus, WITHOUT codex-spark, and it does not inherit Pro's 5x/20x multipliers — a Business seat has Plus-sized headroom for fan-out. A common planning error is assuming the paid-team tier buys concurrency.

Codex — Enterprise/Edu and bring-your-own-key: model availability "follows the API models available to your key"; flexible-pricing workspaces have no fixed rate limits and scale with credits. With a BYO key you "Pay only for the tokens Codex uses, based on API pricing" — the ceiling becomes org rate limits and budget rather than a 5-hour window, which is the only configuration where per-lane model choice is a pure cost question.

Codex — per-agent binding (the mechanism a tiered policy needs): agent files at ~/.codex/agents/<name>.toml or .codex/agents/<name>.toml take `model` and `model_reasoning_effort`, and "If a custom agent file sets model or model_reasoning_effort, the value in the file takes precedence." Global [agents] keys: enabled (default true), max_concurrent_threads_per_session, default_subagent_model, default_subagent_reasoning_effort. Session controls: /model, /effort, --model/-m, --reasoning-effort/-e.

Gemini CLI — maximum model requests per user per day: Gemini Code Assist (Individual) 1,000; Google AI Pro 1,500; Google AI Ultra 2,000; Code Assist Standard 1,500; Code Assist Enterprise 2,000; Gemini API key free/unpaid 250 and "Model requests to Flash model only"; paid API key and Vertex "Varies". Two things matter for agent design: one prompt can be dozens of model requests, and model availability is "across the Gemini model family as determined by Gemini CLI" — per-model selection is not plan-gated, the CLI chooses.

Gemini CLI — model selection lags the API materially. The CLI's valid-model set does not include gemini-3.6-flash or gemini-3.5-flash-lite, still hardcodes gemini-2.5-pro as DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL (a model with an announced 2026-10-16 shutdown) and gemini-3-pro-preview in its picker (shut down 2026-03-09). Selection surfaces: --model/-m (highest precedence) → GEMINI_MODEL → project settings → user settings; per-subagent via agents.overrides.<agentName>.modelConfig.model, since /model "does not override the model used by sub-agents".

xAI / Grok Build CLI — plan gating is NOT documented on any reachable xAI page: x.ai/news and x.ai/build/changelog return 403 to fetchers and docs.x.ai/build/overview states no subscription requirement. Consumer Gemini app — Free gets gemini-3.6-flash as the new default plus a limited daily allotment of 3.1 Pro; AI Pro (~$19.99) adds Gemini 3 Pro access and Antigravity at basic limits (4x free limits); AI Ultra adds Deep Think / Gemini Spark at up to 20x Pro limits. Relevant only as a signal of which model a non-API teammate is actually talking to.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: Agent tool per-invocation `model`; subagent frontmatter `model` (sonnet|opus|haiku|fable | full id | `inherit`, the default); `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` env default; `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (v2.1.257+) to override every definition. Resolution order (v2.1.251+): per-invocation `model` → definition frontmatter `model` (where `inherit` = the main conversation) → `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` → the main conversation's model. NOTE THE REVERSAL: before v2.1.251 the env var came FIRST and overrode both the per-invocation parameter and the frontmatter — this registry carried that older order until 2026-09-05, so any lane logic written against it had the priority inverted. Setting the env var to `inherit` is the same as leaving it unset.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: subagent and skill frontmatter `effort` (low|medium|high|xhigh|max, available levels per model) — overrides the session level while that subagent or skill runs, but NOT the environment variable; session-level `--effort` at launch · `/effort` · `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`. There is no per-subagent *thinking* setting: since v2.1.198 a subagent inherits the main conversation's extended-thinking configuration. VERIFY, don't assume: `/tasks` names the model each running subagent is on and adds the effort level when the subagent definition or the skill it forked from sets `effort` (v2.1.242+) — that is the cheapest check that a lane binding actually applied. `/effort s` (v2.1.257+) scopes an effort change to the current session only, matching `/model`.
harnessBinding.concurrency: default 20 subagents per session (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`); ultracode sessions are exempt from that limit.
caveats: Default effort is high on every effort-capable model except Opus 4.7 (xhigh).

Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 hold a first-run default-effort choice across sessions; the vendor states Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 have no such hold. Since v2.1.257 `--effort` lifts a held model's hold for that session only rather than permanently, and an effort picked on claude.ai for a Remote Control session applies during the hold.

`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` is a DEFAULT, not a pin — a definition's `model` or a model Claude passes per invocation both beat it (v2.1.251+). Only `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (v2.1.257+) makes it win, and while FORCE is on Claude Code ignores every definition's `model` field including the built-in Explore and Plan agents and Claude cannot pass a model at spawn; setting FORCE alone (no model) puts every subagent on the main conversation's model. Two lanes escape FORCE anyway: a conversation fork, and a skill run in a subagent with `model: inherit`. Blocked-by-allowlist values no longer fall through silently in every case: since v2.1.222 a blocked FAMILY alias runs on the newest permitted version of that family, other blocked values fall back to the inherited model, and interactive sessions print a warning naming both models — headless/scripted lanes are where the substitution is still unannounced.

The built-in Explore agent inherits the main conversation's model (since v2.1.198, no longer forced to Haiku) but ON THE CLAUDE API IT IS CAPPED AT OPUS — a Fable-5.1 main session runs Explore on Opus 5, not on Fable, and a Sonnet or Haiku session runs Explore on that same model. On Bedrock / Google Cloud / Microsoft Foundry / Claude Platform on AWS there is no cap and Explore inherits directly. To put exploration on a cheap lane, define a user or project subagent named `Explore` with `model: haiku` — it overrides the built-in and keeps its own `model` field. Plan inherits with no cap; statusline-setup is fixed to Sonnet and claude-code-guide to Haiku.

Enterprise admins can cap maximum effort per model per role; with json/stream-json output or in background agents the clamp applies SILENTLY, so a scripted lane can run below its requested effort with no signal.

Frontmatter `model:` on custom commands and skills was IGNORED in interactive sessions until 2.1.259 fixed it — a lane binding written as command/skill frontmatter and «verified» on a build before 2.1.259 was never actually exercised. The same release also stopped auto mode from running a turn on a model it does not support when frontmatter named one (it now keeps the session model). Re-verify any guard that assumes frontmatter enforcement against a build ≥ 2.1.259.

2.1.261 added `--append-subagent-system-prompt-file` (read the subagent system prompt from a file, for prompts too large for the command line) — a per-lane configuration surface that does not appear in perLaneModel/perLaneEffort and is invisible to any guard that only inspects the invocation's `model`/`effort` arguments. 2.1.261 also added `bashOutputMaxChars` / `taskOutputMaxChars` (up to 128K inline before spooling to a file), which changes how much a fan-out lane's output costs the parent, and 2.1.260 removed the one-hour time limit on background commands started by subagents.

ultracode cannot be set through `effortLevel` or `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, and an env level other than `xhigh` leaves ultracode's workflow orchestration inactive with no signal — a scripted ultracode lane can run as plain effort.

Before v2.1.260, `model: fable` subagents ignored the `[1m]` tag on an `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` pin and ran at 200K silently, and Fable 5.1 prompt caching did not cover context attached after tool results — both are pre-2.1.260 correctness and billing faults, not model behavior.

ultracode is a SESSION setting, not a lane setting: the Agent tool has no per-invocation effort, so a Fable lane under an ultracode session inherits xhigh unless its definition sets `effort`; Workflow `agent()` opts.effort is the per-lane knob. Verify with `/tasks` (v2.1.242+), which names each running subagent's model and its effort when the definition or skill set one — assert observed behavior, not requested settings.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: agent files at `~/.codex/agents/<name>.toml` or `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` with `model`; global `[agents] default_subagent_model`; session `codex agents` (0.150.0, «Allow session configuration with `codex agents`»). DEFAULT MODEL MOVED: since 0.153.4 (2026-09-04) GPT-6 Astra is the bundled default «when no model is explicitly configured» — an unbound Codex lane now bills at $10/$50. Bind every lane explicitly; do not reason from «the Codex default is 5.6».
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: same agent file with `model_reasoning_effort`; global `[agents] default_subagent_reasoning_effort`; session `/model`, `--model/-m`, `--reasoning-effort/-e`. For scripted lanes, `codex exec` also carries `-o, --output-last-message <FILE>`, `--json` (print events to stdout as JSONL) and `--output-schema <FILE>` (JSON Schema for the final response shape) — all three confirmed on the installed 0.153.4 binary's own `--help`, none of them new in the 0.150.1→0.153.4 span (no changelog entry adds them).
harnessBinding.concurrency: `[agents] max_concurrent_threads_per_session` («Cap concurrently open spawned-agent threads, excluding the primary»), `[agents] enabled` (default true), and `[agents] interrupt_message` («Record a model-visible message when an agent turn is interrupted»).
caveats: Precedence: a custom-agent file value wins; otherwise explicit spawn value → the `[agents]` default → the parent value.

Effort value sets differ across vendor pages (subagents page lists low..max/ultra; config reference lists minimal..xhigh) — treat the exact allowed set as per-model and verify against the model you bind.

Observability arrived before the guard did: 0.153.0 added nullable `model` and `reasoningEffort` fields to app-server thread metadata, so a lane's ACTUAL bound model and effort are now readable rather than assumed — use it to verify bindings instead of trusting the config. 0.151.0 «Kept tool availability and reasoning effort correct when switching models or falling back to another model» — i.e. before 0.151.0 a fallback could leave a lane running at the wrong effort with the wrong tool set, silently. 0.151.0 also «Counted nested subagent token usage toward root goal budgets», so a nested fan-out that previously looked free against a budget now charges the root.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: subagent frontmatter — only `name`, `description`, `model` (default `inherit`), `readonly`, `is_background`. Bracket-option syntax carries the knobs: `composer-2.5[fast=false]`, `claude-opus-5[effort=high,context=300k]`.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: via the bracket parameter `effort` (also `fast`, `context`) — no separate effort field.
caveats: Auto Cost bills a flat per-million rate independent of the model that serves the request; Auto Balance / Auto Intelligence bill at the actual model rates and third-party models add a Cursor Token Rate.
Max Mode "API rate plus 20%" is scoped to legacy request-based plans only.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: `agents.overrides.<agentName>.modelConfig.model` — `/model` does NOT change the model used by subagents. Selection precedence for the main lane: `--model/-m` → `GEMINI_MODEL` → project settings → user settings.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: no harness-level effort tier. Per-lane budget dials are the subagent schema fields instead: `kind`, `tools`, `mcpServers`, `temperature`, `max_turns`, `timeout_mins`.
harnessBinding.concurrency: not documented as a single key; day quotas are per plan (see planGating).
caveats: The CLI's valid-model set lags the API materially — it can still default to and offer models the API has shut down. Pin explicitly rather than trusting the picker.
Google deprecated temperature / top_p / top_k in the Gemini API (2026-07-21 changelog), leaving thinking_level as the determinism knob.

Re-measured 2026-09-05, UNCHANGED: `DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL = 'gemini-2.5-pro'` and `DEFAULT_GEMINI_FLASH_MODEL = 'gemini-2.5-flash'` are still the CLI's hardcoded defaults (`DEFAULT_GEMINI_FLASH_LITE_MODEL = 'gemini-3.1-flash-lite'`), and gemini-3.6-flash, 3.7-flash and 3.8-flash are ALL absent from VALID_GEMINI_MODELS — three consecutive Flash releases missing, so treat every new Flash as API-only for this harness until a release note says otherwise. NOTE the 2.5-family shutdown that the 2026-07-25 sweep dated 2026-10-16 is NOT on Google's deprecations page as of 2026-09-05 (gemini-2.5-pro / -flash / -flash-lite all read «No shutdown date announced»), so the defaults are stale but not on a known clock — pin explicitly anyway. harnessBinding.perLaneModel: `[secondary_model]` — a second model pointer beside `default_model`, intended for spawning subagents at lower cost; accepts `model`, `default_effort` and the same patch fields as model overrides.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: `default_effort` on the model pointer; K3 accepts `reasoning_effort` low|high|max (default high).
caveats: `model_preference` accepts only `primary`/`secondary` — it never names a concrete model alias, so a lane picks a *pointer*, not a model.
Docs warn that K3 / K2.7 without Thinking routes to K2.6 — a silent cross-model reroute.

harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: unverified. opencode documents `reasoningEffort` only as a provider passthrough example, and LiteLLM does not explicitly document pinning `reasoning_effort` per deployment.
caveats: Treat per-lane effort at the router layer as unproven until measured on the actual provider+model pair.

prop.why: 도구 호출 사이의 짧은 진행 메모는 thinking 블록으로 오는데 기본 display "omitted" 에선 비어 있어요 — 안 요청하면 사용자에게 아예 안 닿아요. beta thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18. 그 위에 사람이 보는 UI 라면 «시작 한 줄 · 중간 갱신 · 마무리 요약» 문장을 system 에 넣어요(이 워크스페이스의 좌석 프롬프트가 이미 그 문장이에요).

evidence.note: 「Set display: "updates" (beta, thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18 header) and render each non-empty thinking block as a status line」 + 「Before you start, say in a line what you're about to do; brief updates while you work help the user follow along. Close with a short recap …」

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — 무인 레인엔 «자율 실행 + 범위=요청» 두 블록
prop.why: 목표가 분명하면 아주 긴 작업을 방법론 지시 없이 완주하지만, 비동기 작업에서 «다음엔 …하겠다» 로 턴을 끝내거나 이미 요청된 단계를 «적용할까요?» 로 되묻는 경향이 있어요. 첫 문장(사용자가 지켜보고 있지 않다)이 효과의 대부분이고 그대로 써야 해요. 부작용: 모호한 요청에도 덜 물어요 — 사람이 붙어 있는 레인엔 넣지 마세요.

evidence.note: 「You are operating autonomously. The user is not watching in real time … Stop only for destructive actions or genuine scope changes the user must decide」 + 「The opening sentence … carries much of the effect. Keep it as written」 + 「# Delivering work — The user's request … sets the scope, and the scope is the deliverable」

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — 클라이언트측 compaction 요약엔 «보존 항목 6종» 지시
prop.why: 이 모델은 «요약이 무엇을 남겨야 하나» 를 명시하면 잘 따라요. 서버측 compaction 은 이미 그렇게 하고, 클라이언트에서 접으면 공급사 문장을 그대로 써요 — 어려움과 해결 · 시도/보류한 선택지 · 결정·제약·선호(원문대로) · 현재 위치 · 미결·약속 · 재구성 어려운 세부(이름·숫자·날짜·링크). 사용자의 말은 원문 가까이, 모델의 설명은 결론으로 압축.

evidence.note: 「Summarize the transcript inside <summary></summary> tags … Be sure to preserve: (1) any difficulties or problems … (6) specific details that would be hard to reconstruct … Weight the two voices differently」

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — «요청 밖은 고치지 말고 보고» + «테스트는 요청/관례만큼만» 한 단락
prop.why: 열린 기능 요청에서 인접 코드를 고치거나 동작을 확장하거나 테스트 파일을 필요 이상 커밋하는 경향이 있어요. 공급사 단락을 넣으면 «과제 성공률 변화 없이» 여분과 커밋 테스트가 크게 줄어요.

evidence.note: 「If, while working or testing, you find a pre-existing bug … don't fix, optimize or extend it in this change … Commit tests only where the task asks for them or this repository already keeps tests for this kind of change」 + 「unrequested additions and committed test code drop substantially with no measurable change in task success」

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — 파일 편집엔 «전체 재작성 말고 국소 편집» 한 줄
prop.why: Fable 5 보다 작은 변경에도 파일 전체를 다시 쓰는 경향이 있어요. 결과는 같지만 출력 토큰·시간이 늘어요. 한 줄로 Fable 5 수준으로 돌아와요.

evidence.note: 「The number of tokens used to edit files is best minimized, all else being equal. Therefore, when it will not affect the end result, try to surgically edit a file rather than rewrite the entire thing.」

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — low effort 레인엔 «이름을 알아본다 ≠ 현재 상태를 안다» 검색 유도, 또는 그 턴만 effort 상향
prop.why: low 에서 검색·검색형 도구를 Fable 5 보다 덜 부르고 기억으로 답해요. 신선한 정보가 필요한 턴은 per-message effort(beta)로 그 턴만 올리거나 공급사 문장으로 검색을 유도해요 — 이 레지스트리처럼 «빠르게 움직이는 영역(AI 모델·개발 도구)» 을 다루는 레인이 정확히 그 경우예요.

evidence.note: 「At low effort, Claude Fable 5.1 is less likely than Claude Fable 5 to call a search or retrieval tool, and more likely to answer from memory」 + 「When a query centers on a name you do not confidently recognize, or recognize from a fast-moving area like AI models and developer tools … search before answering」

avoidFor.role: 보안 점검 레인 — 공격자 시뮬레이션 · 레드팀 · 익스플로잇/공격도구 관련 작업
avoidFor.why: Fable 5 와 같은 stop_details 범주의 분류기가 돌아요. 완화된 점 하나: «Fable 5 출시 때보다 오탐이 적고, 소스코드의 취약점 찾기는 허용» 이라고 공급사가 명시해서 **방어적 점검(취약점 탐지)은 이제 보낼 수 있어요.** 그러나 공격형 기법(익스플로잇·멀웨어·공격 도구)은 여전히 거절→폴백(cyber → Opus 4.8) 대상이라, Ultrasafe 의 attacker/redteam 스킬 레인은 계속 여기로 안 보내요. 오탐을 키우는 세 조건(컴파일 확인 문구 · 마이너 언어 · 도구 출력의 base64)은 피할 수 있어요.

evidence.note: 「Claude Fable 5.1's safety classifiers produce fewer false positives than Claude Fable 5's did at launch, and finding vulnerabilities in source code is permitted. False positives still occur」 + 세 조건(compile-check phrasing · lesser-known languages · base64 in tool output)
「safety classifiers covering the same stop_details categories as Claude Fable 5 … The permitted fallback targets for Claude Fable 5.1 are Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Opus 5」
Claude Code fallback table — Fable 5.1 and Fable 5: Cybersecurity → Opus 4.8, Biology → Opus 5

shed.claim: 예시 뭉치 — 문체·톤을 맞추려고 20개씩 넣던 부류
shed.why: 1차: 공급사 문서가 예시 **개수**를 다루지 않아요. 인접 항목(「기존 스킬이 이 모델엔 과도하게 처방적이라 품질을 떨어뜨릴 수 있으니 덜어 보라」)은 있지만 그건 *지시* 이야기지 *예시* 이야기가 아니에요 — 이웃 주장의 근거를 이 주장에 붙이지 않아요. 2차(2026-08-02 합산): 공통 best-practices 는 개수를 **직접** 다뤄요 — 3~5개면 충분하고 5개 초과는 수확 체감. 같은 문서가 「문체·톤은 서술보다 예시가 가장 신뢰됨」이라고도 하니, 이 확정의 뜻은 **«예시 0» 이 아니라 «뭉치(20)를 3~5 로»** 예요 — 그 이상으로 읽으면 근거 밖이에요.

evidence.note: 원 관측 — 단일 관측자
「Three to five examples are usually sufficient … diminishing beyond five」 — 개수를 직접 다루는 유일한 1차 문서. 단 같은 문서가 문체·톤 맞춤엔 예시가 최선이라 명시 — 지지 범위는 «20개 뭉치는 과잉» 까지
「strongest raw writer … with no style guidance it already has more edge and fewer clichés」 — 기본 문체가 강해 뭉치 의존이 준다는 별도 도메인 관측

shed.claim: 추론 재현 지시 — 「생각한 과정을 응답에 적어라」류
shed.why: 이 모델에선 그런 지시가 **거부 범주를 유발**해서 다른 모델로의 폴백이 늘어요. 스킬·시스템 프롬프트에 남아 있으면 조용히 비용이 돼요. 우리 쪽 스킬도 감사 대상이에요.

evidence.note: 「Don't instruct Claude to reproduce its reasoning in the response … can trigger the reasoning_extraction refusal category … causing elevated fallbacks」

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — **명시적 자기검증 + 신선한 문맥의 검증 서브에이전트**
prop.why: **Opus 5 와 정확히 반대예요.** 이 모델에는 자기검증을 명시하라고 하고, 자기비판보다 «신선한 문맥의 별도 검증 서브에이전트» 가 낫다고 해요. 같은 장치가 한 모델엔 지울 것이고 다른 모델엔 붙일 것 — 모델별 프로필이 필요한 이유가 추측이 아니라 문서 대조로 나온 자리예요.

evidence.note: 「Make self-verification explicit in long-run prompts. Separate, fresh-context verifier subagents tend to outperform self-critique.」 ↔ Opus 5 의 「do not use subagents to verify」 와 정반대

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — 진행 주장을 도구 결과에 대조시키기 · 문맥 잔량 수치를 모델에 노출하지 않기
prop.why: 장기 자율 실행에서 진행 보고를 지어내는 경향이 있고, 남은 토큰 카운트다운을 보여 주면 스스로 새 세션을 제안하거나 작업을 줄여요.

evidence.note: 「Before reporting progress, audit each claim against a tool result … nearly eliminated fabricated status reports」 + 「Avoid surfacing explicit context-budget counts where possible」

advisorFor.why: **반증됨.** 공급사는 이 모델을 「가장 요구가 큰 추론과 장기 에이전틱 작업용」으로 자리매김해요 — 문체 모델이 아니에요. 오히려 프롬프팅 문서에 «사용자에게 읽히는 글» 을 위한 별도 교정 지침이 붙어 있어요(밀도 높은 축약·화살표 사슬을 쓰는 경향). 표현의 권위가 아니라 표현에 **도움이 필요한** 쪽이에요.

evidence.note: 「Anthropic's most capable widely released model, built for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work」 — 문체·톤 특화라는 자리매김이 없음
「Readability when communicating with the user」 절 — 이 모델이 읽기 어려운 글을 내는 경향에 대한 완화 지침

avoidFor.role: 보안 점검 레인 — 공격자 시뮬레이션 · 레드팀 · 익스플로잇/공격도구 관련 작업
avoidFor.why: 이 모델의 안전 분류기가 **공격형 보안 기법**(익스플로잇·멀웨어·공격 도구 제작)을 겨냥하고, 문서가 **선의의 보안 작업도 걸릴 수 있다**고 명시해요. 우리 Ultrasafe 모듈은 스킬 이름부터 web-api-attacker · ai-llm-redteam · social-engineer 이고 관련 어휘가 138곳이라, 그 레인을 이 모델로 돌리면 체계적으로 거부→폴백이에요. 공급사 권장 완화도 폴백 구성이라, 애초에 그 레인을 여기로 안 보내는 게 맞아요. **적용 시점**: 8종 팬아웃은 2026-07-28 회차로 이미 한 번 돌았고(열린 발견 92건), 그 게이트는 resolved 예요 — 그러니 이건 **다음 회차(차단 모드 전환 심사)** 에 거는 제약이에요. 지난 회차가 영향받았는지는 **알 수 없어요**: 회차 원장이 시각·공격자 목록·해시만 들고 모델을 안 실어서, 어느 에이전트가 거절돼 폴백됐는지 사후 복원이 안 돼요.

evidence.note: 「safety classifiers that target offensive cybersecurity techniques (such as building exploits, malware, or attack tooling) … Benign cybersecurity work and beneficial life sciences tasks may also trigger these safeguards」 + 폴백 구성 권장
「Claude Fable 5 includes safety classifiers that can decline requests」 — refusal 은 200 응답으로 오고 어느 분류기가 거절했는지 보고됨

shed.claim: 판단 사안을 절대 규칙으로 굳힌 도구 사용 규칙 — 「질문에 '최신'이 있으면 검색하라」류
shed.why: 공급사가 **「when to search」를 판단 사안의 예시로 직접 이름 대면서** 절대 규칙 대신 decision rule 을 쓰라고 해요. 다만 「도구 규칙을 다 없애라」가 아니에요 — 안전·필수 필드 같은 **진짜 불변**에는 절대 규칙이 맞고, 판단 사안만 굳히지 말라는 거예요. 원 주장을 그 폭으로 좁혔어요.

evidence.note: 「Avoid unnecessary absolute rules. Use ALWAYS, NEVER, must, and only for true invariants … For judgment calls, such as when to search, ask, use a tool, or keep iterating, prefer decision rules.」
원 관측 — 단일 관측자

advisorFor.role: 교차 분석 — 다른 훈련 계보의 반박
advisorFor.why: 공급사 문서가 다룰 만한 주제가 아니에요(자기 모델을 남의 고문으로 권할 이유가 없어요). 근거를 찾으려면 커뮤니티·비교 벤치 쪽이라 2차 조사 대상이에요.

shed.claim: 승인 게이팅 — 단계를 쪼개 하나씩 사람 확인을 받게 하던 부류
shed.why: 세 계보 문서가 각각 같은 방향이에요. 모델이 이미 안정적으로 하는 거동에 절차 지시를 붙이지 말 것(OpenAI), 멈출 자리를 일일이 열거할 필요 없이 「정말 사람이 필요한 때만 멈춰라」 한 줄이면 됨(Fable), 범위는 제약하되 순서는 맡길 것(Opus). **검증 장치와 헷갈리지 마세요** — 그건 모델마다 반대예요.

evidence.note: 제거 대상 목록에 「process instructions for behavior the model already performs reliably」
「Pause for the user only when the work genuinely requires them … there is no need to enumerate every case」

harnessProfile.researchLog: 1차 조사(2026-08-02): 공급사 1차 문서 5종 정독. 확증 3 · **반증 2** · 미확정 2. 반증이 나온 게 이 계약의 값이에요 — 지웠으면 다음 조사가 같은 자리를 처음부터 다시 발견했을 거예요. 커뮤니티·SNS 합산은 아직 안 돌렸어요(공급사 문서만으로 A급이 나와서 2차로 미룸). 2차 합산(2026-08-02): 남은 미확정 1건(Fable 예시 뭉치)에 개수를 직접 다루는 공통 문서(A) + 별도 도메인 관측(D)을 얹어 confirmed — 뜻은 «예시 0» 이 아니라 «뭉치를 3~5 로». Opus 재주입 refuted 는 계약대로 유지. 이로써 1차가 남긴 미확정 대기열은 비었어요.
